summary: Intermittent p50 latency jump for US-east pinned traffic caused by keepalive/edge handoff during residency refresh
description: Issue summary: Customer reports periodic P50 latency spikes for requests pinned to us-east despite overall throughput and P95 remaining stable. Impact: Intermittent customer-facing slowdowns for chat completions and embedding lookups during control-plane residency refresh windows. Environment: Dedicated pool for ClarityHealth in prod-us-east; single-tenant reserved capacity with token-level residency stamps enabled. Observed window: spikes occur in short bursts (~10-30s) roughly aligned with pin refresh cadence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer API key scoped to ClarityHealth dedicated pool (token-scoped residency enabled).
2) Send steady stream of small completion requests and periodic embedding requests (approx 50 rps).
3) Observe p50 latency for requests over a 30 minute window and correlate with control-plane pin refresh timestamps.
4) Note: issue reproduced only when client connections are long-lived (HTTP keepalive) and when pin TTL refresh occurs during active connections.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:05:20Z edge-proxy[proxy-12] INFO connection-hand-off user=ClarityHealth token=tok_XXX src_ip=34.201.1.22 dest=us-east-edge-3 reason=pin_refresh
2026-03-10T14:05:21Z routing-service WARN route-change user=ClarityHealth old_path=us-east-edge-3 new_path=us-east-edge-7 latency-delta=220ms
2026-03-10T14:05:21Z serving-runtime INFO request-id=abc123 model=open-llm-13b-v2 exec_ms=45 total_ms=340
Client-side metric sample: p50 increased from 120ms baseline to 340ms during handoff window; p95 ~ unchanged (420ms -> 460ms).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: pin refresh causes control-plane to rotate residency stamp which triggers soft-handoff between edge proxies; long-lived keepalive connections may get proxied to a new edge that requires a TLS rehandshake or route reconnection leading to added 150-250ms on p50.
Correlation found between control-plane 'pin_refresh' events (every 15m by default for this account) and observed p50 spikes in request logs.

Observed that requests using HTTP/1.1 keepalive (no re-open) still experienced routing change at edge (proxy-level stream reattach) which added an extra hop: edge -> new-edge -> serving, compared to normal edge -> serving path.
No evidence of GPU contention or scheduler queueing during the spike windows (serving-runtime exec_ms unchanged).
DNS resolution times stable; TLS handshake logs show an increase in short-lived rehandshakes tied to the proxy handoff window.
Temporary replication of the problem in staging by forcing pin refresh confirmed the handoff reproduces p50 delta when connections are long-lived.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports P50 jumps to ~300-350ms during 'rotation' windows. They see this across small completion and embedding calls. They are concerned about user impact for chat UX.

Arjun Patel (SRE) 2026-03-11: I reproduced in staging by triggering a pin refresh and keeping connections open. Logs show proxy handoff adds ~200ms due to short-lived TLS rehandshake and extra routing hop. Raising to control-plane to discuss pin refresh behavior.

Lena Ortiz (Control Plane) 2026-03-11: Current pin refresh is implemented as a soft-rotate to balance control-plane leases. We can consider keeping connection affinity for active keepalive sessions until the session idle timeout to avoid immediate handoff. Filing INT-4472 for a control-plane change proposal.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-12: Shared preliminary findings with customer and suggested workarounds. Customer requests a short-term mitigation and asks for timeline for a permanent fix.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation provided: advised customer to set client keepalive timeout < 30s to force client reconnection outside of pin refresh window OR set pin TTL to a longer value on their dedicated config to stagger refreshes (support can apply a temporary TTL override on their account).

Workaround applied for ClarityHealth: Support extended pin TTL for their dedicated pool to 60m for the next 72 hours (temporary config change) — reduced observed p50 spikes in monitoring by >80% during the next rotation window.

Long-term plan: INT-4472 created to change control-plane behavior to avoid breaking affinity for active keepalive connections; control-plane engineering to propose one of: a) honor active connection affinity until session idle, b) perform zero-downtime in-proxy transfer without TLS rehandshake, or c) coordinate rotation during low-traffic windows.

Follow-ups: assign control-plane owner to INT-4472, update runbook for residency pin rotations, and include a KB article describing recommended client keepalive and pin TTL settings for dedicated customers.
